cards.statement: Azure Monitor collects resource logs automatically when an Azure resource starts generating them.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor resource logs need a diagnostic setting for collection. Include log routing in the design before relying on these logs for troubleshooting.
cards.misconception: Resource logs are collected automatically as soon as a resource emits them.

source.title: Resource logs in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Azure Monitor diagnostic settings can route resource logs through Azure Event Hubs to a non-Microsoft SIEM.
cards.explanation: Azure Event Hubs provides the documented streaming destination for sending Azure Monitor resource logs to external SIEM systems.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Diagnostic settings support central log routing to a workspace in another subscription with suitable access.
cards.explanation: A diagnostic setting may target another subscription when its configuring user has appropriate access to both. This supports centralized logging across subscriptions.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Diagnostic settings can preserve metric dimensions when exporting platform metrics to a Log Analytics workspace.
cards.explanation: Diagnostic settings flatten multidimensional metrics and aggregate across dimension values. Use another collection path when the analysis needs that breakdown.
cards.misconception: Diagnostic exports retain the dimensional breakdown available in native metrics.

source.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor

cards.statement: A Log Analytics workspace stores incoming logs in the region of the resource that emits them.
cards.explanation: Log data resides in the workspace's region. Choose the workspace location to meet the workload's data residency requirements.
cards.misconception: Workspace data stays in the source resource's region regardless of the workspace location.

source.title: Design a Log Analytics workspace architecture

cards.statement: Resource-context access can isolate teams' resource logs within a shared Log Analytics workspace.
cards.explanation: Resource-context access limits a resource owner's queries to logs for resources they can access. A shared workspace can therefore serve separate application teams.

source.title: Design a Log Analytics workspace architecture

cards.statement: Basic tables in Azure Monitor Logs support simple log alerts for data that needs occasional investigation.
cards.explanation: The Basic plan reduces ingestion cost for medium-touch logs while supporting simple log alerts. It suits data retained for occasional troubleshooting.
cards.volatilityNote: Table-plan query and alert capabilities are evolving.

source.title: Azure Monitor Logs overview

cards.statement: Auxiliary tables offer the same interactive query performance as Analytics tables in Azure Monitor Logs.
cards.explanation: Auxiliary queries are slower and suit low-touch audit or compliance data. Analytics provides optimized query performance for frequent operational analysis.
cards.misconception: Auxiliary provides Analytics-level query performance at a lower ingestion cost.

source.title: Azure Monitor Logs overview

cards.statement: The instrumentation key in an Application Insights connection string acts as a security key against forged telemetry.
cards.explanation: The instrumentation key only identifies the Application Insights resource and isn't a security key. To reject unauthenticated telemetry, disable local authentication and require Microsoft Entra ID.
cards.misconception: The instrumentation key in a connection string protects ingestion like a secret key.

source.title: Connection strings in Application Insights - Azure Monitor

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication checks on-premises sign-in hours when validating passwords.
cards.explanation: Pass-through authentication validates credentials against on-premises Active Directory at sign-in. It enforces the directory's permitted sign-in hours at that point.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Pass-through authentication automatically switches to password hash synchronization during an on-premises outage.
cards.explanation: Administrators manually switch pass-through authentication to password hash synchronization. Prepare synchronization before an on-premises outage.
cards.misconception: Enabling password hash synchronization makes authentication failover automatic.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Federation supports cloud sign-in with sAMAccountName when an organization retains DOMAIN\username logins.
cards.explanation: A requirement to use sAMAccountName, such as DOMAIN\username, calls for federated authentication. Microsoft Entra ID's native hybrid sign-in options use other supported identifiers.

source.title: Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra External ID uses an external tenant for B2B guests who access employee applications.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Entra External ID places B2B collaboration guests in the workforce tenant containing employee applications. An external tenant serves consumer and business-customer applications.
cards.misconception: Business collaboration guests belong in an external tenant because they are external users.

source.title: Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID

cards.statement: A user-assigned managed identity lets replacement virtual machines reuse the same authorized identity.
cards.explanation: A user-assigned managed identity exists independently of the virtual machines using it. Replacing those machines preserves the identity and its permissions.

source.title: What is managed identities for Azure resources?

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access trusts B2B guests' home-tenant MFA claims by default.
cards.explanation: Initial cross-tenant access settings exclude trust in another tenant's MFA claims. Administrators enable inbound MFA trust to let those claims satisfy their Conditional Access policies.
cards.misconception: A guest's successful home-tenant MFA automatically satisfies the resource tenant's MFA requirement.

source.title: Overview: Cross-tenant access with Microsoft Entra External ID

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra application proxy uses Kerberos constrained delegation for single sign-on to IWA apps.
cards.explanation: For web applications using Integrated Windows Authentication, the private network connector uses Kerberos constrained delegation to authenticate users to the application.

source.title: Microsoft Entra application proxy

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Domain Services can extend an on-premises domain with Microsoft-managed domain controllers.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services creates a standalone managed domain. It offers legacy domain protocols for Azure workloads rather than extending the existing on-premises domain.
cards.misconception: The managed domain controllers become additional controllers in the existing on-premises domain.

source.title: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Azure RBAC for Azure Key Vault data-plane access to secrets, keys and certificates.
cards.explanation: Azure RBAC centralizes Azure Key Vault access and separates permission management from vault administration. Microsoft recommends it over the legacy access policy model.

source.title: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) vs. access policies (legacy)

cards.statement: Azure Key Vault renews a certificate from a nonintegrated certificate authority as the certificate nears expiry.
cards.explanation: Certificates from a nonintegrated certificate authority need an external signing and merge process for renewal. Azure Key Vault provides expiration notifications for them.
cards.misconception: Importing a certificate gives Key Vault built-in renewal integration with its issuing authority.

source.title: Renew your Azure Key Vault certificates

cards.statement: A management group can govern subscriptions that trust different Microsoft Entra tenants together.
cards.explanation: Subscriptions in a management group trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant. A cross-tenant organization needs a governance design that respects that boundary.
cards.misconception: Management groups provide a single hierarchy across Microsoft Entra tenants.

source.title: What are Azure management groups?

cards.statement: Cost Management tag inheritance copies resource group tags onto the resources in the group.
cards.explanation: Tag inheritance applies subscription and resource group tags to child resource usage records, not to the resources themselves, so costs can be grouped without tagging every resource.
cards.misconception: Enabling tag inheritance writes the parent tags onto each resource.

source.title: Group and allocate costs using tag inheritance - Microsoft Cost Management

cards.statement: Azure Policy automatically applies additions to an initiative through its existing assignments.
cards.explanation: When an architect adds policy definitions to an initiative, its existing assignments include them. Teams can expand a governance baseline while keeping its assignment structure.

source.title: Overview of Azure Policy

cards.statement: An Azure Policy exemption can end a temporary waiver automatically on its scheduled expiration date.
cards.explanation: A policy exemption records an accepted compliance exception. At its expiration, Azure Policy stops honoring the waiver while retaining the exemption object for records.

source.title: Azure Policy exemption structure

cards.statement: A custom Azure Policy definition in one subscription supports assignments in a separate subscription.
cards.explanation: A custom policy definition stored in a subscription is available for assignments within that subscription. A separate subscription falls outside its definition scope.
cards.misconception: The definition location has no effect on where a custom policy can be assigned.

source.title: Understand scope in Azure Policy

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management supports approval before eligible users activate Azure resource roles.
cards.explanation: Privileged Identity Management can hold an eligible Azure resource role activation for a designated approver's decision, giving architects a human approval gate for elevated access.

source.title: Configure Azure resource role settings in Privileged Identity Management

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra access reviews directly remove denied members from groups synchronized from on-premises.
cards.explanation: Access review results leave membership in on-premises-origin groups unchanged. Administrators need a process that applies denied membership decisions in the source directory.
cards.misconception: Applying access review results changes membership in synchronized on-premises groups.

source.title: Complete an access review of groups and applications in access reviews

cards.statement: Different request policies in one entitlement management access package can grant different resource roles.
cards.explanation: Access package policies vary eligibility, approval and lifecycle settings. Users assigned the package receive its resource roles, so different role bundles need different packages.
cards.misconception: Each request policy in an access package selects a different resource-role bundle.

source.title: Create an access package in entitlement management

cards.statement: Microsoft Entra lifecycle workflows can invoke Azure Logic Apps to perform custom employee offboarding tasks.
cards.explanation: Lifecycle workflows use custom task extensions to run Azure Logic Apps when employee lifecycle requirements extend beyond built-in tasks.

source.title: Lifecycle Workflows custom task extension

cards.statement: Azure SQL Managed Instance supports native cross-database queries between databases on the same instance.
cards.explanation: Native cross-database queries within an instance let an existing application retain this SQL Server dependency in a managed service.

source.title: What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?

cards.statement: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server offers its PgBouncer connection pooler on the Burstable compute tier.
cards.explanation: Built-in PgBouncer is available in the General Purpose and Memory Optimized compute tiers. A Burstable design needs a different connection-pooling solution.
cards.misconception: Built-in connection pooling is available across the flexible server compute tiers.
tags: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

source.title: PgBouncer in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database supports reservation discounts for databases that use the DTU purchasing model.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database reservations apply to the vCore purchasing model. A DTU database design does not qualify for this compute discount.
cards.misconception: Reservation discounts apply equally to the DTU and vCore purchasing models.

source.title: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database serverless can bill active idle databases for less compute than their configured minimum.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database serverless applies the configured minimum vCores and memory to compute billing while the database remains active, even when demand falls below those levels.
cards.misconception: Serverless billing follows low utilization below the configured minimum while a database stays active.

source.title: Serverless compute tier for Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database General Purpose stores persistent data files separately from its compute nodes.
cards.explanation: General Purpose keeps database files in remote Azure Blob storage. Storage latency therefore matters when evaluating a workload for this tier.

source.title: vCore purchasing model - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database Business Critical supports In-Memory OLTP tables for transaction-heavy applications.
cards.explanation: The Business Critical tier includes In-Memory OLTP support, so a design that depends on memory-optimized tables can retain that capability.

source.title: In-memory technologies in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale ties a named replica's compute size to the primary replica's compute size.
cards.explanation: A Hyperscale named replica has its own service level objective. Architects size its compute independently for the read workload it serves.
cards.misconception: Named replicas inherit the primary replica's compute sizing.

source.title: Hyperscale secondary replicas

cards.statement: Always Encrypted grants Azure SQL Database administrators plaintext access through database permissions alone.
cards.explanation: Always Encrypted separates database administration from key access. Reading protected column values also needs access to the column master key outside the database.
cards.misconception: Database administrator permissions are sufficient to decrypt Always Encrypted columns.

source.title: Always Encrypted

cards.statement: Dynamic data masking can hide Azure SQL Database query results from users in the db_owner database role.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database users in db_owner see original values despite dynamic data masking. Masking limits exposure to nonprivileged users.
cards.misconception: Dynamic data masking protects column plaintext from database owners.

source.title: Dynamic data masking

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database enables TDE with a service-managed key by default for new empty databases.
cards.explanation: New empty Azure SQL databases use service-managed transparent data encryption by default, protecting database files and logs against offline access.

source.title: Transparent data encryption for SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB supports Strong consistency in an account configured for multiple write regions.
cards.explanation: Azure Cosmos DB excludes Strong consistency from accounts with multiple write regions. A design using multiple write regions selects a weaker consistency level.
cards.misconception: Strong consistency is compatible with an Azure Cosmos DB account that accepts writes in multiple regions.

source.title: Consistency level choices in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB supports multi-document transactions across shards of a sharded collection.
cards.explanation: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB limits multi-document transactions to a single unsharded collection. Cross-shard transactions need a different design.
cards.misconception: RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB preserves MongoDB transaction support across shards.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported MongoDB API transaction capabilities can expand as the service evolves.

source.title: Supported features and syntax in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB 6.0 server version

cards.statement: An Azure Cosmos DB read with Bounded staleness consistency skips the integrated cache and costs backend RUs.
cards.explanation: The integrated cache serves only Session and Eventual reads, at zero RU on a hit. Strong, Bounded staleness and Consistent prefix reads are served from the backend and use RUs.

source.title: Integrated Cache - Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Azure Data Lake Storage gives analytics jobs atomic directory renames when the account uses a hierarchical namespace.
cards.explanation: A hierarchical namespace changes a directory entry during a rename instead of processing its blobs individually, reducing the work needed to publish analytics output.

source.title: Azure Data Lake Storage hierarchical namespace

cards.statement: Azure Files serves SMB and NFS clients simultaneously through the same share when a workload needs both protocols.
cards.explanation: An Azure file share uses SMB or NFS. Workloads needing both protocols use separate shares, even when the shares reside in the same storage account.
cards.misconception: An Azure file share can expose the same files concurrently through SMB and NFS.

source.title: Plan an Azure Files deployment

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends RA-GZRS for storage accounts needing maximum availability and durability.
cards.explanation: RA-GZRS keeps a geographically separate copy for regional recovery, matching Microsoft's maximum availability and durability guidance.
cards.volatilityNote: Microsoft's recommended redundancy choice can change as storage options evolve.

source.title: Azure storage disaster recovery planning and failover

cards.statement: Azure Table storage lets an architect define secondary indexes on non-key entity properties.
cards.explanation: Azure Table storage indexes the partition and row keys. For other frequent lookup paths, the application maintains alternate entities or its own index entities.
cards.misconception: Azure Table storage offers native secondary indexes on arbitrary entity properties.

source.title: Design Azure Table storage for queries

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage blocks an app from creating a new version when an earlier version has an immutability policy.
cards.explanation: Version-level immutability protects the selected version. An application can write a new version of the blob while the earlier protected version remains intact.
cards.misconception: Immutability on a blob version freezes future writes to the blob's version history.

source.title: Data protection overview

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage lets a logging app add records to an immutable append blob with protected append writes enabled.
cards.explanation: Protected append writes permit new blocks at the end of an append blob while preserving its immutability. Existing blocks remain protected from changes.

source.title: Container-level WORM policies for immutable blob data

cards.statement: Azure Blob Storage releases a legal hold when the compliance team's retention interval expires.
cards.explanation: A legal hold remains in effect until an authorized user explicitly clears it. It suits retention whose end date is unknown.
cards.misconception: A legal hold expires on a scheduled retention deadline.

source.title: Immutable storage for blob data overview

cards.statement: A private on-premises data source can feed Azure Data Factory copy activity through a self-hosted integration runtime.
cards.explanation: A self-hosted integration runtime runs inside the private network and moves data between reachable private sources and cloud stores.

source.title: Integration runtime in Azure Data Factory

cards.statement: A self-hosted integration runtime lets Azure Data Factory run mapping data flow transformations on its host.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory executes mapping data flows on managed Spark clusters supplied by the Azure integration runtime.
cards.misconception: A self-hosted integration runtime executes mapping data flows locally.

source.title: Integration runtime in Azure Data Factory

cards.statement: A managed private endpoint in Azure Data Factory reaches a storage account only after the account's owner approves it.
cards.explanation: Creating a managed private endpoint opens a Pending private endpoint connection. The storage account owner approves or rejects it, and only an approved endpoint can send traffic.

source.title: Managed virtual network and managed private endpoints - Azure Data Factory

cards.statement: An Azure Data Factory schedule trigger can backfill missed time intervals when an ingestion pipeline resumes.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Factory uses tumbling window triggers for historical backfill. Schedule triggers handle current or future runs.
cards.misconception: Schedule triggers retain missed intervals for historical backfill.

source.title: Pipeline execution and triggers in Azure Data Factory or Azure Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: In-flight dedicated SQL pool queries keep running while Azure Synapse Analytics scales the pool's compute.
cards.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics cancels dedicated SQL pool queries when scaling is requested and rolls back open transactions before changing compute resources.
cards.misconception: Dedicated SQL pool compute scaling preserves query execution.

source.title: Manage compute in a dedicated SQL pool

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics serverless SQL pool bills each query by the data it processes rather than by its run time.
cards.explanation: Serverless SQL pool reserves no resources and charges only for the data that queries process, which suits occasional exploration of data lake files.

source.title: Serverless SQL pool - Azure Synapse Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Stream Analytics queries Azure SQL Database reference data afresh upon arrival of an incoming event.
cards.explanation: Azure Stream Analytics joins events against an in-memory snapshot of Azure SQL Database reference data. It refreshes that snapshot at a configured interval.
cards.misconception: Azure SQL Database reference joins retrieve live database values for each event.

source.title: Use reference data for lookups in Stream Analytics

cards.statement: Azure Data Explorer automatically reprocesses pre-existing source rows when an architect creates an update policy.
cards.explanation: Azure Data Explorer update policies react to newly ingested data. An architect handles existing source rows through a separate backfill.
cards.misconception: Creating an update policy retroactively transforms existing source data.

source.title: Update policy overview

cards.statement: Azure Synapse Analytics lets Spark jobs finish while autoscale decommissions nodes during a scale-in operation.
cards.explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics marks scale-in candidates for decommissioning, then lets running Spark jobs finish before removing the nodes.

source.title: Automatically scale Azure Synapse Analytics Apache Spark pools

cards.statement: Fabric Data Warehouse can persist analytical tables in SQL Server's native database file format for sharing.
cards.explanation: Fabric Data Warehouse stores tables in Delta format: Parquet data files with a transaction log. This format supports sharing data across analytical tools.
cards.misconception: Fabric Data Warehouse uses SQL Server database files because it offers a SQL Database Engine surface.
cards.volatilityNote: Microsoft Fabric is evolving rapidly; its storage architecture and interoperability options may change.

source.title: What is Fabric Data Warehouse?

cards.statement: For on-premises VMware recovery, Azure Site Recovery's latest processed point favors shorter recovery time.
cards.explanation: The latest processed recovery point skips processing replicated data that is still pending, reducing failover time when restoring an on-premises VMware VM.

source.title: Run VMware VMs failover to Azure

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery recovery plans can invoke Azure Automation runbooks to coordinate application recovery.
cards.explanation: A recovery plan can run Azure Automation runbooks during failover to Azure, automating application-specific tasks that would otherwise slow recovery.

source.title: About recovery plans

cards.statement: Azure Site Recovery fails over the machines inside one recovery plan group one at a time.
cards.explanation: Machines in one recovery plan group fail over in parallel. Order applies between groups: Group 2 machines start failing over only after every Group 1 machine has failed over and started.
cards.misconception: Machines within a recovery plan group fail over sequentially.

source.title: About recovery plans in Azure Site Recovery

cards.statement: An immutable vault in Azure Backup protects operational blob backups from destructive changes.
cards.explanation: Azure Backup vault immutability excludes operational blob backups. Its protection applies to recovery points held in the vault, rather than operational recovery points.
cards.misconception: Vault immutability extends to operational blob recovery points.

source.title: Immutable vault for Azure Backup

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database point-in-time restore can rewind the original database to undo an application's data corruption.
cards.explanation: Point-in-time restore creates a new Azure SQL Database. An administrator then decides how to use the restored database to recover the application.
cards.misconception: Point-in-time restore overwrites the original database in place.

source.title: Restore a database from a backup in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database long-term retention backups remain available after an administrator deletes the logical server.
cards.explanation: Azure SQL Database retains long-term retention backups after logical-server deletion. Administrators can restore them to another server in the same subscription.

source.title: Long-term retention backups

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database geo-restore depends on available target-region capacity at the time of recovery.
cards.explanation: Geo-restore provisions a database from geo-replicated backups when requested. A regional disaster can increase demand, so available target-region capacity affects recovery.

source.title: Restore a database from a backup in Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB continuous backup automatically protects a single-region account against regional disaster.
cards.explanation: Azure Cosmos DB continuous backups need another account region for resilience against regional disaster. Enabling continuous backup alone does not provide that protection.
cards.misconception: Continuous backup automatically places recoverable copies outside a single account region.

source.title: Continuous backup with point-in-time restore in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Azure Files vaulted backups can recover a share after the source share and its snapshots become unavailable.
cards.explanation: Azure Files vaulted backups keep offsite recovery data. Azure Backup can restore the share to an alternate location even when the source snapshots are unavailable.

source.title: About Azure Files backup

cards.statement: Azure Storage automatically retains geo-redundancy after a customer-managed planned failover to the secondary region.
cards.explanation: Customer-managed planned failover leaves the storage account geo-redundant as GRS. The original primary becomes the new secondary, retaining a geographically separate copy.

source.title: Azure storage disaster recovery planning and failover

cards.statement: Azure automatically recreates a zonal virtual machine in a healthy zone when its original zone fails.
cards.explanation: A zonal Azure virtual machine remains tied to its zone. Customers design redundant capacity in other zones instead of relying on automatic cross-zone recreation.
cards.misconception: Azure automatically replaces standalone zonal virtual machines in another zone during a zone outage.

source.title: Reliability in Azure Virtual Machines

cards.statement: Azure App Service automatically attempts to replace lost instances after a zone fails in a zone-redundant plan.
cards.explanation: App Service backfills instances on a best-effort basis during a zone outage. A capacity requirement that survives zone loss calls for provisioning spare capacity ahead of time.

source.title: Reliability in Azure App Service

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database failover groups let applications reuse listener addresses after a geo-failover.
cards.explanation: Failover-group listener names stay fixed while Azure updates their DNS targets. An application reconnects through the same listener address.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: A Business Critical secondary created by an Azure SQL Database failover group automatically inherits zone redundancy.
cards.explanation: A failover group creates a Business Critical secondary with zone redundancy disabled by default. Configure that secondary's zone redundancy separately.
cards.misconception: Failover groups propagate a Business Critical primary's zone-redundancy setting to a newly created secondary.
cards.volatilityNote: Default propagation of zone-redundancy settings when Azure creates a secondary may change.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Microsoft-managed failover policy for Azure SQL Database failover groups.
cards.explanation: Microsoft recommends customer-managed policy so the customer controls when to fail over an affected group.
cards.misconception: Microsoft recommends delegating Azure SQL Database failover decisions to the service.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Database

cards.statement: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server can serve reporting queries from its high availability standby.
cards.explanation: The flexible server HA standby stays in recovery mode until promotion and rejects application read queries. Reporting needs a separate read-serving design.
cards.misconception: The PostgreSQL high availability standby also provides reporting capacity.
tags: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

source.title: High availability in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

cards.statement: Azure SQL Managed Instance failover groups replicate all user databases in an instance as one failover unit.
cards.explanation: A Managed Instance failover group covers the instance's user databases together. This scope matters when applications need independent database failover boundaries.

source.title: Failover groups overview & best practices - Azure SQL Managed Instance

cards.statement: Azure Cosmos DB commits writes locally in a satellite region of a multi-region write account.
cards.explanation: A satellite region acknowledges writes after a local quorum commits them. Azure Cosmos DB sends them to the hub asynchronously for conflict resolution.

source.title: Multi-region writes in Azure Cosmos DB

cards.statement: Azure Files can serve reads from a geo-redundant account's secondary region before account failover.
cards.explanation: Geo-redundant Azure file shares become accessible in the secondary region after account failover. Read-access storage redundancy does not expose a secondary file-share endpoint.
cards.misconception: A geo-redundant account makes its secondary Azure file shares readable before failover.

source.title: Data redundancy in Azure Files

cards.statement: An Azure Spot Virtual Machine evicted under the Deallocate policy keeps incurring storage charges for its disks.
cards.explanation: Deallocate, the default eviction policy, stops the VM but keeps its disks, which stay billed while the VM counts against quota. The Delete policy removes the disks together with the VM.

source.title: About Azure Spot Virtual Machines - Azure Virtual Machines

cards.statement: Azure Dedicated Host gives a regulated workload exclusive use of the datacenter's physical network.
cards.explanation: Azure Dedicated Host isolates the physical compute server. Its network and underlying storage infrastructure remain shared with other hosts.
cards.misconception: Dedicated compute hardware also provides a customer-exclusive physical datacenter network.

source.title: Azure Dedicated Hosts

cards.statement: Azure Container Apps lets platform teams directly manage deployments through the Kubernetes API.
cards.explanation: Azure Container Apps abstracts the Kubernetes API. A requirement for direct Kubernetes API access points to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).
cards.misconception: The managed Kubernetes foundation of Azure Container Apps exposes its Kubernetes API to customers.

source.title: Comparing Container Apps with other Azure container options

cards.statement: Azure CNI Overlay conserves virtual network addresses by assigning AKS pods a separate address range.
cards.explanation: Azure CNI Overlay assigns pod addresses from a range separate from the node subnet. This reduces the virtual network address space a large AKS deployment consumes.

source.title: CNI networking in Azure Kubernetes Service

cards.statement: Azure Container Instances can provide full orchestration for applications needing coordinated multi-container scaling.
cards.explanation: Azure Container Instances runs containers rather than supplying a full orchestration platform. A coordinated scaling requirement needs another orchestration design.
cards.misconception: Azure Container Instances includes the orchestration needed for a coordinated container application.

source.title: Choose an Azure compute service

cards.statement: Azure Functions Premium can end its compute charges by releasing its idle plan's remaining instances.
cards.explanation: An active Azure Functions Premium plan retains a minimum billed allocation even when its apps are idle. Budgeting must account for that standing compute cost.
cards.misconception: Azure Functions Premium scales its active plan to zero billed compute during idle periods.

source.title: Azure Functions Premium plan

cards.statement: Azure Functions Flex Consumption can reach private dependencies through virtual network integration.
cards.explanation: Flex Consumption connects function apps to services secured within a virtual network, meeting private-resource access requirements within its serverless hosting model.

source.title: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan hosting

cards.statement: The Azure Functions Premium plan supports custom Linux containers for workloads with packaged dependencies.
cards.explanation: The Premium plan accepts custom Linux container deployments, so the workload can bring the runtime environment its dependencies need.

source.title: Azure Functions Premium plan

cards.statement: Azure Functions lets an architect extend the HTTP response deadline by increasing the function execution timeout.
cards.explanation: Azure Functions enforces an HTTP response limit separately from execution timeout. Long processing can use an asynchronous response pattern instead.
cards.misconception: A longer function execution timeout also lengthens the HTTP request's response window.
cards.volatilityNote: HTTP response limits and their relationship to execution timeouts can change with Azure Functions hosting.

source.title: Azure Functions hosting options

cards.statement: Azure Batch adds a scheduling-service charge to the compute resources a parallel processing workload consumes.
cards.explanation: Azure Batch charges for underlying resources such as compute, storage, and networking. The Batch scheduling service adds no separate charge.
cards.misconception: Azure Batch adds a separate service fee for managing job scheduling.

source.title: What is Azure Batch?

cards.statement: Azure Service Bus requires sessions to guarantee FIFO processing within a workflow's related message groups.
cards.explanation: Azure Service Bus sessions keep related messages under one receiver's exclusive lock. This enables ordered processing of a workflow's message sequence.

source.title: Azure Service Bus message sessions

cards.statement: Azure Event Hubs supports a global arrival order guarantee across partitions for a partitioned telemetry stream.
cards.explanation: Ordering in Azure Event Hubs applies within a partition. An architect keeps related events in the same partition when processing depends on their arrival order.
cards.misconception: Azure Event Hubs preserves arrival order across separate partitions.

source.title: Event Hubs features and terminology

cards.statement: Azure Event Grid subject filters let a subscriber select blob events from a chosen container in a storage account.
cards.explanation: Azure Event Grid uses the event subject's container path to filter storage events before delivering them to a subscriber.

source.title: Event filtering in Azure Event Grid

cards.statement: The Azure Storage queues service moves a message that keeps failing into a dead-letter queue.
cards.explanation: A consumer of Azure Storage queues checks a message's DequeueCount and implements its own policy for moving poison messages to a dead-letter queue.
cards.misconception: Azure Storage queues provide automatic poison-message isolation.

source.title: Storage queues and Service Bus queues compared and contrasted

cards.statement: Azure API Management Premium supports gateways in multiple Azure regions within the same service instance.
cards.explanation: Azure API Management Premium deploys regional gateways for geographically distributed callers. Its management plane remains in the primary region.
cards.volatilityNote: Azure API Management tier capabilities evolve as v2 offerings gain features.

source.title: Deploy an Azure API Management instance to multiple Azure regions

cards.statement: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway stops serving APIs when its connection to Azure fails.
cards.explanation: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway continues using its in-memory configuration during a temporary Azure connection loss. Configuration updates and cloud telemetry pause.
cards.misconception: A self-hosted gateway requires continuous cloud connectivity to process API traffic.

source.title: Self-hosted gateway overview

cards.statement: Azure Managed Redis automatically rebuilds an in-memory cache from enabled persistence after node failures.
cards.explanation: Persistence restores the same Azure Managed Redis cache from its latest persisted state. Recovery can lose writes that have not yet reached persistence.

source.title: Configure data persistence for an Azure Managed Redis instance

cards.statement: Azure App Configuration stores different values for the same key by using environment labels.
cards.explanation: Azure App Configuration identifies values by the combination of key and label. Environment labels let applications select their own variant from a shared store.

source.title: Understand Azure App Configuration key-value store

cards.statement: Azure App Configuration can copy a secret's value into its store through a Key Vault reference.
cards.explanation: Azure App Configuration stores a URI for a Key Vault reference. The application authenticates to Azure Key Vault and retrieves the secret's value.
cards.misconception: A Key Vault reference duplicates the secret inside Azure App Configuration.

source.title: Use Key Vault references in an ASP.NET Core app

cards.statement: Read access to a template spec grants a release team the rights to create the spec's resources in a resource group.
cards.explanation: Read access lets a team use a template spec without being able to change it. Creating its resources also needs the permissions for deploying an ARM template at the target scope.
cards.misconception: Template spec read access also grants the right to deploy the resources it describes.

source.title: Create & deploy template specs - Azure Resource Manager

cards.statement: Azure deployment stacks can relinquish management of a resource that an operations team intends to keep running.
cards.explanation: An architect selects detachment when removing a resource from a deployment stack's template. Azure keeps the resource and removes it from the stack's managed set.

source.title: Create and deploy Azure deployment stacks in Bicep

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager preserves omitted properties when an incremental template includes an existing resource.
cards.explanation: An incremental Azure Resource Manager deployment reapplies an included resource's properties. Omitted properties can reset to defaults, so the template describes the intended final state.
cards.misconception: An incremental deployment merges supplied properties into an existing resource while retaining omitted values.

source.title: Azure Resource Manager deployment modes

cards.statement: One Cloud Adoption Framework workload landing zone holds a workload's development, test and production environments.
cards.explanation: Each workload gets a single workload landing zone with all its environments, each made of one or more subscriptions that inherit the platform landing zone's guardrails.

source.title: What is an Azure landing zone? - Cloud Adoption Framework

cards.statement: The Cloud Adoption Framework delays Secure work until an organization completes the Adopt phase.
cards.explanation: The Secure methodology applies across the Cloud Adoption Framework, including strategy, planning, readiness, and adoption. Teams integrate security during adoption.
cards.misconception: An organization completes workload adoption before it begins the Cloud Adoption Framework's security work.

source.title: Secure overview

cards.statement: Azure Migrate can estimate post-migration compute and storage costs from its Azure VM sizing recommendations.
cards.explanation: An Azure VM assessment calculates estimated running costs after it establishes readiness and sizing. Architects use this projection when comparing migration designs.

source.title: Assessment overview (migrate to Azure VMs)

cards.statement: Azure Migrate Collector collects a discovery snapshot in an on-premises network with restricted Azure connectivity.
cards.explanation: The Collector scans the estate locally and exports inventory for later upload. Discovery therefore suits environments where continuous Azure connectivity is impractical.
cards.volatilityNote: The Collector's supported discovery environments can expand.

source.title: Discover servers and workloads using Azure Migrate collector

cards.statement: For VMware vSphere, Azure Migrate uses guest-installed migration agents when it reuses its discovery appliance.
cards.explanation: The VMware vSphere migration path using the discovery appliance is agentless. Replication proceeds through VMware snapshots and changed block tracking instead of guest agents.
cards.misconception: The migration path that reuses Azure Migrate's discovery appliance still needs migration agents inside VMware guest VMs.

source.title: Agentless and agent-based migration methods

cards.statement: Azure Database Migration Service in the Azure portal supports online migration to Azure SQL Database.
cards.explanation: The Azure portal version of Azure Database Migration Service provides an offline migration path to Azure SQL Database. The migration design accounts for downtime.
cards.misconception: The Azure portal version of Azure Database Migration Service provides an online path for Azure SQL Database.
cards.volatilityNote: The service's supported migration paths can expand.

source.title: What is Azure Database Migration Service?

cards.statement: Azure Database Migration Service in the Azure portal migrates SQL Server logins along with the databases.
cards.explanation: The Azure portal version of Azure Database Migration Service migrates schemas and data but not logins, so the migration plan moves logins to the target separately.
cards.misconception: Azure Database Migration Service carries logins over with the databases it migrates.

source.title: What Is Azure Database Migration Service?

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database retains TDE protection inside a BACPAC file exported for a database migration.
cards.explanation: Exporting a TDE-protected Azure SQL Database produces an unencrypted BACPAC. A migration design needs separate protection for that exported data.
cards.misconception: TDE encryption follows the database data into its exported BACPAC file.

source.title: Transparent data encryption

cards.statement: Azure Storage Mover can catch up on-premises file changes after Azure Data Box seeds the migration target.
cards.explanation: Storage Mover compares the local source with the seeded target and transfers differences before cutover, shrinking the final online transfer.

source.title: What is Azure Storage Mover?

cards.statement: Migrating file shares from sites on three continents takes one Azure Storage Mover resource per continent.
cards.explanation: One Azure Storage Mover resource can manage migrations from source shares anywhere in the world; for agent-based migrations, an agent near each source share sends data directly to Azure.
cards.misconception: Azure Storage Mover needs a separate resource for each geography that hosts source shares.

source.title: Introduction to Azure Storage Mover

cards.statement: Azure Traffic Manager can move an established client connection to another region when an endpoint fails.
cards.explanation: Traffic Manager influences DNS answers for subsequent connections. Clients connect directly to endpoints, so an existing connection recovers through client reconnection.
cards.misconception: Traffic Manager's regional failover transfers live client connections.

source.title: How Traffic Manager works

cards.statement: Azure Application Gateway's TLS listener passes the client's TLS session unchanged to the backend.
cards.explanation: A TLS listener terminates the client's TLS session at Application Gateway. The gateway creates a separate connection to the selected backend.
cards.misconception: Application Gateway's TLS proxy preserves the client-to-backend TLS session.

source.title: Application Gateway TCP/TLS proxy overview

cards.statement: Azure Load Balancer routes public TCP and UDP workloads through a global endpoint across regional deployments.
cards.explanation: Azure Load Balancer's global topology fronts regional load balancers through a shared public endpoint for transport-layer traffic.

source.title: Global load balancer - Azure Load Balancer

cards.statement: The ExpressRoute Premium add-on extends a circuit's Azure connectivity beyond its geopolitical region.
cards.explanation: ExpressRoute Premium adds connectivity across geopolitical boundaries, meeting a design that connects an on-premises network to more distant Azure deployments.

source.title: ExpressRoute overview

cards.statement: Azure Virtual WAN supports VPN-to-ExpressRoute branch transit through its Standard hubs.
cards.explanation: A Standard virtual WAN hub router lets VPN-connected sites and users reach ExpressRoute-connected sites when the Branch-to-branch setting is on and BGP is used; Basic offers site-to-site VPN only.

source.title: Azure Virtual WAN Overview

cards.statement: Azure App Service evaluates an app's access restriction rules for traffic that arrives through a private endpoint.
cards.explanation: App Service sends traffic from a private endpoint straight to the app without evaluating access restriction rules; network security groups restrict traffic to private endpoints.
cards.misconception: A private endpoint on an App Service app closes its public endpoint.

source.title: Use Private Endpoints for Apps - Azure App Service

cards.statement: Azure virtual network service endpoints can authorize Azure service access for traffic originating on-premises.
cards.explanation: Service endpoints identify Azure virtual network subnets. On-premises requests need a different access design because they do not use that subnet identity.
cards.misconception: Service endpoints extend subnet authorization to on-premises traffic.

source.title: Virtual network service endpoints

cards.statement: Azure Firewall Premium meets a requirement to inspect the payload of outbound HTTPS traffic.
cards.explanation: Azure Firewall Premium's TLS inspection acts as a forward proxy, decrypting outbound HTTPS before re-encrypting it for the destination.

source.title: Azure Firewall Premium features

cards.statement: Azure NAT Gateway automatically translates internet-bound traffic to fixed public IPs that partners can allowlist.
cards.explanation: NAT Gateway uses configured static public IP addresses or prefixes for outbound traffic. Partners can allowlist that predefined address set instead of individual workload addresses.

source.title: What is Azure NAT Gateway?

cards.statement: Azure Application Gateway WAF can inspect HTTP requests received through its TCP or TLS proxy listeners.
cards.explanation: Azure Application Gateway WAF v2 can host TCP/TLS proxy listeners, but those listeners bypass WAF inspection. Use HTTP(S) listeners to inspect web requests.
cards.misconception: A WAF-enabled gateway inspects HTTP payloads on its TCP/TLS proxy listeners.
cards.volatilityNote: Inspection support for TCP and TLS proxy listeners may expand as this capability evolves.

source.title: Application Gateway TCP/TLS proxy overview

cards.statement: Enabling DDoS IP Protection on a public IP also protects other public IPs in the same virtual network.
cards.explanation: DDoS IP Protection applies to the public IP address where it is enabled. Other addresses need their own protection coverage even when they share a virtual network.
cards.misconception: IP-level DDoS protection spreads to neighboring public IPs in the virtual network.

source.title: Reliability in Azure DDoS Protection
